chapter: Will Marion Cook and the Southern Syncopated Orchestra
title: Bechet leaves with Benny Peyton; Buddy Gilmore
summary: Bechet joined Benny Peyton's Jazz Kings; Briggs describes Peyton as a schooled percussionist and Buddy Gilmore as a showman drummer who worked with Vernon Castle.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Well, had Bechet stayed with Lattimore, or did he go with Cook?
No, no, he didn't stay with Lattimore. Bechet had gotten out with Benny Peyton's group, Benny Peyton formed the Jazz Kings and --
Okay, we had a little fire whistle going by. It was hard to hear.
Okay, so now Bechet, he went off and formed a different group all together, and that was with Benny Peyton and he is a drummer.
Yes, he's a drummer, yes.
Right.
And it was his group.
Benny Peyton was not the drummer of the orchestra, he was a
Briggs
tympanist percussionist.
Right, I see. He was a schooled musician?
Yes, schooled musician.
And Buddy Gilmore was a drummer. He had a drum solo. He did a drum solo.
In the Syncopated Orchestra?
Yes.
He was a snare drummer?
He was a snare drummer, and traps. Snare and traps.
Right. I see.
He was the guy that worked with Vernon Castle, that famous dance team, Vernon Castle, and Buddy Gilmore was with him.
And he, now just to stay with Buddy Gilmore for a minute. He was a New York guy too, was he?
Briggs
Yes, but -- yes, he was originally from New York, he was one of the Clef Club. He used to play gigs, and that --
But he wasn't so much of a jazz musician in that sense, as a straight drummer?
No, no, he was both. He invented something --
He played jazz too.
He invented something, he'd go to a table with his sticks and shave one's head, and cut hair -- wonderful, he was simply wonderful.
Just go around the back of your head with the sticks.
With the sticks, with a razor or something, you know.
Make kind of a razor noise behind your head?
Well, he was a terrific showman. He was more of a showman. But artistic
Briggs
as well. He was a good drummer.
Yes.
I mean he had a background. I don't know whether it was reading. Whether you could call him a pit drummer or something. That I don't know.
Benny Peyton, yes. Benny Peyton was a reader, reading drummer. As a matter of fact he was also in the 15th.
He was?
He was in the 15th, yes.
So Benny Peyton and Bechet, and who else was in that group?
Joe Caulk, banjo.
Cork?
Caulk. C-a-u-l-k.
He was also of the Syncopated Orchestra. And we had Pierre de Caillaux on piano, George Jones on violin, Fred Coxito on alto-saxophone and that's about all. Benny Peyton on drums.
